US-119-HR10183.title: SRBIJA Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

US-119-HR10183.description: To authorize certain actions with respect to Serbia.
US-119-HR10183.aiSummary: This bill would set U.S. policy toward Serbia and call for sanctions on people who the President says hurt peace, democracy, human rights, or anti-corruption efforts in the Western Balkans. It would require reports and a strategy on Russian and Chinese influence in Serbia, and it would limit U.S.-Serbia strategic talks unless key issues like elections, corruption, and press freedom are addressed. The bill would also allow more U.S. help for Serbia only after the President certifies that Serbia has made major progress, and it would end five years after enactment.

US-119-HR9150.title: Boxing Therapy for Parkinson’s Access Act
US-119-HR9150.summary:
Boxing Therapy for Parkinson's Access Act

This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to furnish boxing-based exercise classes to veterans who (1) are enrolled in the VA health care system, (2) have been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (or a similar movement disorder), and (3) elect to participate in such classes to treat the disease or disorder.
US-119-HR9150.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-06-04)

actions.text: Referred to the Subcommittee on Health.
Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

US-119-HR9150.aiSummary: The bill would require the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide boxing-based exercise classes to enrolled veterans who have Parkinson’s disease or a similar movement disorder and choose to join. It would apply to veterans in the VA health care system. The classes would be for treatment of that condition.

US-119-HR9194.title: Build American Efficiency Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

US-119-HR9194.description: To clarify the evidentiary treatment of documentation generated under a qualifying process standard for purposes of compliance with the Build America, Buy America Act, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9194.aiSummary: The bill would let the Housing and Urban Development secretary treat certain paperwork made under a named process standard as enough proof that a project meets domestic content rules under the Build America, Buy America Act. It applies to HUD financial aid and to funding recipients who must show their materials meet U.S. content requirements. It would also let HUD accept similar standards if they provide a checkable and verifiable process.
